Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10

Topic 1.3: Leadership Development
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Leadership Development, part of Citizenship 1.2 Community Needs (9 Lessons) By the end of the sub strand the lea in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can one become an effective leader?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Leadership Development together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: Learners show a concerted attention to detail while developing the simple CSL guidelines to govern

CSL activities.

● Learning to Learn: Learners carry out research on attributes and skills of a good leader and present in class.

Values:
Integrity: Learners adhere to laid down procedures in the guidelines as they elect leaders for different roles for their

CSL group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Good governance: Learners develop attributes of good governance as they elect leaders for roles in their CSL activities.

Suggested learning resources:

Digital devices with assistive technology, audio visual clips of documentaries, braille reference materials, print

reference materials with appropriate font and colour contrast, print and braille learner’s books, braille and print writing

materials.
